leakage_control.note: in_fold: the univariate association step is performed inside each training fold, so no test patient influences which features enter the model. none: reproduces the original submission, in which that step had been applied to the whole cohort.

reproducibility_note: Cross-validation partitions are fully determined by random_seed. Classifier internal randomness is deliberately NOT seeded (random_state=None): seeding it would make every repeat see the same bootstrap sample for a given fold, correlating the repeats and producing artificially narrow variance on fold-averaged metrics. Point estimates are stable across runs; the last digit of a per-fold metric may vary.

cv_design.methods_paragraph: Prediction performance was evaluated by repeated stratified nested cross-validation. The outer loop was stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 20 times with different random partitions (100 outer test-fold evaluations; each outer training set comprised ~80% of patients and each held-out test fold ~20%). Within every outer training fold, stratified 5-fold inner cross-validation was used for classifier selection, hyperparameter tuning and feature-signature discovery; all preprocessing (imputation, near-zero-variance filtering, correlation pruning, scaling, the univariate outcome screen) was fitted on outer training patients only. Arm-specific models used 5-fold outer cross-validation repeated 100 times (500 evaluations per arm) with 3-fold inner cross-validation. No shuffle-split resampling was used at any stage.
cv_design.figure_legend: Schematic of the repeated stratified nested cross-validation framework. The outer loop is stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 20 times (100 outer evaluations; ~80% training / ~20% testing per fold). Within each outer training fold, stratified 5-fold inner cross-validation performs model selection and feature ranking. The selected model is evaluated on the corresponding held-out outer test fold, and performance is pooled across all 100 outer evaluations.
